clue.text: Bring in navy to intimidate the whole county

indicators.note: to bring something in is to take it inside, so the navy's letters go into the verb for intimidating

parts.note: to cow someone is to intimidate them
RN is the Royal Navy
the whole means all

explanation.surface: Someone calls up the fleet to cow an entire English shire into submission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring in' looks like the harvest, but it is the container signal. CORNWALL is the county at England's far south-western tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornwall is one of the English shires, so it is an example of a county.

clue.text: Author's cooler, having to go into business

indicators.note: to go into means to enter, so the cooler's word is put inside the business abbreviation

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
an icer is something that cools

explanation.surface: A writer's refrigerator is to be brought into the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Author's means 'is'. Cicero was the Roman orator and writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero, the Roman statesman, wrote many speeches, letters and treatises, so he was a writer.

clue.text: Meat market's up for disposal

indicators.note: for disposal suggests being broken up and rearranged, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, with its S

explanation.surface: A market is being put up for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for disposal' rearranges MARKETSUP, the S of market's included.
explanation.definitionFit: Rump steak is a cut of beef from the hindquarters, so it is a meat.

clue.text: Court has Dickens little girl up for made-up yarn

parts.note: to woo is to court

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read upwards, so the girl's name is reversed

parts.note: Little Nell is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop

explanation.surface: A court hears that a Dickens heroine is fabricating a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the girl's name upwards in this down entry. 'Made-up yarn' sounds like a lie but means wool knitted or woven.
explanation.definitionFit: Woollen goods are made from spun wool, so yarn that has been made up into cloth fits.

clue.text: Drug after drinks can make one fall badly

indicators.note: after places the drug's letter behind the drinks' word

parts.note: laps means drinks, as a cat laps milk
E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Taking a drug after drinking can make a person collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: E is slang for ecstasy. 'can make one' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip into bad ways or err is to fall from good behaviour.

clue.text: Be sad about besieging city, such as Leningrad

indicators.note: an army besieging a place surrounds it, so the reversed word goes round the city
about means turned round here, so the word for being sad is read backwards

parts.note: to mope is to be sad and listless
NY is New York, the American city

explanation.surface: Someone grieves over the long wartime siege of the Russian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the sad word round to EPOM before 'besieging' wraps it round the city. The surface leans on the siege of Leningrad, but the city is only an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Leningrad took its title from Lenin, so it is a thing named after a person, which is the sense intended here.

clue.text: Horse has power, that's plain

parts.note: IE stands for id est, Latin for 'that is'
bald means plain or unadorned, as in a bald statement

explanation.surface: A horse is obviously strong.
explanation.walkthrough: IE is the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald is a horse with irregular black and white patches.

clue.text: Girl's love accepted by one chap, head over heels

indicators.note: head over heels means upside down, so in a down clue the whole assembly is read upwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in, so the zero is held inside the chap

parts.note: a man is a chap
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A girl's love is welcomed by a man who is head over heels for her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' puts O inside MAN to make MOAN; I plus MOAN is then turned over by 'head over heels'. The 's of Girl's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female first name, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: Be successful-in frame of mind to consume a lot of beer

indicators.note: to consume is to take in, so the beer goes inside the frame of mind

parts.note: mood is a frame of mind
a keg is a cask holding a quantity of beer

explanation.surface: To prosper, you must be in the mood for a heavy drinking session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to consume' puts the beer inside the mood; 'in' just links the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed, especially after a poor start, is to make good.

clue.text: Letter from minister giving rosy picture of the country

definitions.meaning: a bishop's or clergyman's letter to his flock

definitions.text: giving rosy picture of the country
definitions.meaning: presenting an idealised view of rural life

explanation.definitionFit: A pastor's open letter to his congregation carries this name; idyllic rural poetry and painting is described the same way.

clue.text: Inferior experimental treatment all right to include in collection of notes etc.

parts.note: common can mean inferior or vulgar
a placebo is a dummy treatment given in medical trials
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A second-rate trial drug is approved for inclusion in a scrapbook of jottings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include in' only joins the wordplay to the definition. The pieces run straight through: COMMON, PLACEBO, OK.
explanation.definitionFit: A commonplace book is a personal notebook of quotations, jottings and extracts, i.e. a collection of notes and the like.

clue.text: Decide to have another go at crossword?

explanation.definitionFit: Resolving means firmly deciding; read as re-solve it means working out the puzzle a second time.

clue.text: Detective's job to get copy of picture

definitions.meaning: a detective's task is tracking down people, i.e. following their trail
a copy made by drawing over the lines of an original seen through thin paper

explanation.definitionFit: Following a missing person's trail is the sleuth's work; an outline copied through thin paper is a drawing of the same name.

clue.text: Broadcast listener received in part of Ireland

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of the next word are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio audience member is picked up in an Irish region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' rearranges LISTENER. LEINSTER is the eastern of Ireland's four historic provinces.
explanation.definitionFit: Leinster is one of the four provinces of Ireland, so it is a region of that island.

clue.text: School supplier folds before spring

parts.note: tucks are folds stitched in cloth
to hop is to spring or jump

explanation.surface: A school outfitter puts pleats in garments before springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: A TUCKSHOP is a British school's snack shop, 'tuck' being slang for sweets and food.
explanation.definitionFit: A British school's snack counter sells sweets and food to pupils, so it supplies the school.

clue.text: Food is cooked, holding such a party

indicators.note: the words before holding contain the answer within them, run across their letters

explanation.surface: Food is being cooked for a party that is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' looks like an anagram signal, but 'holding' says the party is hidden inside 'Food is cooked'.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a dance party with recorded pop music, so it is one kind of party.

clue.text: Endless agony, under singular bombardment

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the agony below the singular letter

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
hellfire is the torment of the damned in hell, which lasts for ever

explanation.surface: Unending torment suffered during a unique barrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts HELLFIRE below S in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery shells fired at a target make a bombardment.

clue.text: Do some work in garden, comfortable in retirement here?

definitions.meaning: giving a plot of flowers a drink with a hose or can
retirement means going to bed, and this one is a soft, water-filled place to sleep

explanation.definitionFit: Watering a flower bed is a gardening chore; a bed filled with liquid is a comfortable place to retire at night.

clue.text: Like gardens with odd angles

parts.note: as means like, as in 'as good as'
Kew Gardens is the famous botanical garden in south-west London

explanation.surface: A description of garden beds laid out with eccentric corners.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW Gardens is London's Royal Botanic Gardens, so 'gardens' alone can stand for KEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set crooked, out of line, has odd angles.

clue.text: Wife maybe alters good-for-nothing

indicators.note: maybe means possibly, signalling a possible rearrangement of the next word

explanation.surface: A wife perhaps changes a lazy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges the word after it into the last six letters, behind the wife's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastrel is an idle spendthrift, a person of no use.

clue.text: Commander scowled and looked embarrassed

parts.note: CO is commanding officer
loured (or lowered) means frowned or scowled

explanation.surface: A commanding officer frowned and went red in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: LOURED is an old word for scowled, also spelt lowered.
explanation.definitionFit: To blush is to turn red with embarrassment, so a face that reddened looked embarrassed.

clue.text: Weird bunch missing outside an American city

indicators.note: missing its outside means losing the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: NY is New York

explanation.surface: A strange group goes absent from the edge of a US city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing outside' strips the first and last letters from BUNCH, leaving UNC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eerie and inexplicable is strange or weird.

clue.text: Agreed to cook a sweet

indicators.note: to cook figures is to doctor them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe: everyone agrees to make a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cook' rearranges AGREED.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragée is a sugar-coated sweet such as a sugared almond.

clue.text: Scandalous revelations of model involved in kinky sex

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside, so the model's word sits within the other letters
kinky means twisted, so the letters of the next word are twisted round

parts.note: to pose is to model, as for an artist

explanation.surface: Tabloid scoops about a fashion model caught up in a perverse sex scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kinky' rearranges the scandalous word to EXS, and 'involved in' places the model inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandalous story revealing hidden wrongdoing is an exposé in tabloid language.

clue.text: Friendly pressure put on colleague

parts.note: an ally is a colleague or associate

explanation.surface: A friendly push applied to a workmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' in a down clue places P above ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A pally person is on good terms, i.e. friendly.

clue.text: Expletive with which poet's expelling a rude interrupter

parts.note: heck is a mild expletive

indicators.note: expelling means throwing out, so a letter is dropped from the poet's name

parts.note: Edward Lear is the poet of nonsense verse; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A rude interrupter is thrown out of a poetry reading with a curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expelling' drops the A from LEAR, the nonsense poet, leaving LER; the 's of poet's means 'is'. 'with which' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shouts rude remarks to interrupt a speaker is a barracker of that name.

clue.text: Hercules, young daredevil, repeatedly attacked heads belonging to this

definitions.text: Hercules, young daredevil, repeatedly attacked heads belonging to this

indicators.note: heads means the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: The young Hercules boldly hacked again and again at a monster's many heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' takes the first letters of the five preceding words. The whole clue also describes Hercules fighting the many-headed serpent of Lerna.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Lernaean serpent grew new heads when one was cut off, and Hercules killed it as his second labour.

clue.text: Being poised, holding girl's back and getting in right mood, perhaps, for this?

definitions.text: Being poised, holding girl's back and getting in right mood, perhaps, for this?

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so the next piece goes into the word for being poised

parts.note: balancing means being poised

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter
perhaps signals a variation, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dancer keeps poise, holds a partner's back and gets in the mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' takes in two pieces side by side: the girl's last letter and ROOMD, the rearrangement 'perhaps' makes; 'and getting in' just adds the second. The whole clue describes what the dance needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Poise, holding a partner's back and the right mood are what a formal couple's dance at a grand dance hall requires.

clue.text: Miss one's lines? Clever fish!

parts.note: an actor who forgets lines is said to dry
fly means artful or clever in British slang

explanation.surface: An actor fluffs a speech, and a fish is admired as smart.
explanation.walkthrough: DRY is theatre slang for forgetting lines; FLY is British slang for sharp or knowing. The '!' turns 'fish' into a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry-fly fishing uses an artificial fly that floats on the surface, so to fish that way is a verb sense.

clue.text: It's good to get whatever reward, said cupholder

parts.note: any can mean whatever, as in 'any one you like'

indicators.note: said signals that the word for reward is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: meed is an old word for a reward or deserved share

explanation.surface: Someone claims a prize is good to have, whatever it is.
explanation.walkthrough: MEED, an archaic word for reward, sounds like MEDE. Ganymede was the Trojan youth who served as the gods' cupbearer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Ganymede was the gods' cupbearer, so he literally held their cups.
